note: Read candidate contract for Notion, the priority gated family. This is reference data for the runtime owner, not a profile: no credential appears here, nothing is installed, and no packaged recipe exists. Every value is synthetic.

api_version.documented: Setting this header is required, and the Notion-Version header must be included in all REST API requests so the response is consistent with what the client expects.
api_version.version_changes: At 2026-03-11 the after parameter on Append Block Children becomes a position object, archived becomes in_trash across request parameters and response bodies, and the transcription block type is renamed meeting_notes.
api_version.note: Every fixture in this file is bound to one explicit version. Response shapes are version specific and must not be mixed; the deprecation notes below are what make an unversioned fixture dangerous.

required_static.Authorization: Bearer <integration token supplied by the user>
required_static.documented: The integration sends Authorization: Bearer with its integration token, and Notion-Version is required on every request.

never.path: No credential may appear in a path or query, and no version may be inferred per endpoint.
never.documented: The version is a reviewed request header, not a query default, because the response shape depends on it.

identity_contract.documented: The page is titled Retrieve your token's bot user and states that it retrieves the User associated with the token provided in the authorization header. For a personal access token it returns the user who created the token.

documented_response_fields.object: string, constant user, documented as always present
documented_response_fields.id: string uuid, documented as always present
documented_response_fields.name: oneOf string or null, documented as the name of the user
documented_response_fields.person.email: string, documented as present only when the connection has capabilities that allow access to email addresses
documented_response_fields.bot.owner: object whose type is user or workspace, where a workspace owner means an internal integration
documented_response_fields.bot.workspace_name: oneOf string or null, null when the owner is a user rather than a workspace

limitations: object and id are documented as always present, so the subject is stable.
The documented user object marks name as oneOf string or null, so a bot with no name has no non-empty label. This is the real blocker: the current label contract requires a non-empty label string.
The remaining properties may be absent depending on the connection's capabilities, so no field outside object, id and name may be relied on.

Whether an internal integration token is accepted here is not stated explicitly; the documented bot fields for GET /v1/users/me are the evidence, so a framework test should confirm it with an integration token.
identity_contract.binding_requirement: None. A single-item read takes the object id from the caller, so no identity-derived value is needed in a later path.

smallest_useful_read.documented: Retrieves a database object, which since 2025-09-03 is a container for one or more data sources.

projected_fields.label: id
projected_fields.documented: Required in the documented database object response.

projected_fields.label: title
projected_fields.documented: Required in the documented database object response.

projected_fields.label: url
projected_fields.documented: Required in the documented database object response.

projected_fields.label: parent
projected_fields.documented: Required in the documented database object response; generally a page_id or workspace true.

deliberately_not_projected.reason: Since 2025-09-03 a database response has no properties field at all. Projecting it would describe the deprecated contract, where GET /v1/databases/{id} returned the property schema for versions up to and including 2022-06-28.

properties_schema_read.documented: Since 2025-09-03 the retrieve a data source endpoint is the home of the properties schema for a data source under a database.
properties_schema_read.id_note: A database id cannot be used with the data source route and a data source id cannot be used with the database route; the two id types are not interchangeable.

listing.documented: Querying a data source is a POST with an optional body, and the response is a list object with results, next_cursor and has_more, supporting up to 10,000 results per query.
listing.note: This is a POST read, so listing needs more than the static header. Its paging is a documented cursor, which the current bounded cursor contract already follows.

documented_statuses.400: A missing Notion-Version header fails validation with the documented code missing_version.
documented_statuses.401: The bearer token is not valid, with the documented message API token is invalid.
documented_statuses.403: The token has no access to the resource, with the documented code restricted_resource.
documented_statuses.404: The object was not found or is not shared with the connection, with the documented code object_not_found.
documented_statuses.429: The connection is rate limited, with the documented code rate_limited; 529 is documented alongside it.

failure_document.optional_fields: Some error responses also include an additional_data object with extra context.
failure_document.shape_note: The errors documentation documents the code and message properties and does not document an object, status or request_id envelope, so a framework test must not depend on those fields.

rate_limit_headers.Retry-After: Documented on 429 and 529 responses as an integer number of seconds, and repeated in the body as additional_data.retry_when present.

failure_contract.code_stability: Programmatic error code values such as validation_error and object_not_found are documented as stable and not changing without a version bump.

framework_gap.minimum_missing_behavior: Send one reviewed static header on every request, and accept an identity label that is documented as null. Those two together are what stand between this family and a single-item read.
not_required_for_a_first_read: POST reads, which only block listing a data source.
Any identity-derived path binding, because a database or data source id comes from the caller.
A write: nested v3 templates exist, but no Notion write is proposed in this queue.
framework_gap.not_a_gap: Nothing here requires weakening origin rules, adding a credential to a path, or bypassing the documented version requirement. The header must be sent, not worked around.
